La competición desarrollada en el tramo comprendido entre el mirador de Sicasumbre y Tamaretilla, se convierte en la segunda prueba del calendario majorero de 2026 y los puntos obtenidos cuentan para los campeonatos de Canarias, el Provincial de Las Palmas de RallySprint de asfalto y el certamen insular de la SuperCopa A/T de Fuerteventura.
En la entrega de premios estuvo presente el alcalde, Alejandro Jorge; la presidenta el Cabildo de Fuerteventura, Lola García; el concejal de Deportes, José Benito Alonso; el primer teniente de alcalde, Alexis Alonso; la concejala de Dearollo Local, Lucía Darriba; el consejero de Deportes del Cabildo de Fuerteventura, Luis González, y una representación de la Federación Provincial.
El concejal de Deportes, José Benito Alonso, señaló que “por mi parte objetivo cumplido el traer un evento más para nuestro municipio y destacar el comportamiento ejemplar de los aficionados y la unión de los clubes unidos de Fuerteventura por luchar en la misma dirección por el automovilismo”.
Por otro lado, el primer teniente de alcalde, Alexis Alonso, recalcó la calidad del espectáculo que vieron y afirmó que “desde el Gobierno municipal vamos a pelear por mantener esta prueba el año que viene y, si podemos conseguir algún tramo de tierra, lo hablaremos con las federaciones para lograr incorporarlo”.
Además, el alcalde de Pájara, Alejandro Jorge, aseguró que se trata de “una competición histórica que desde hace muchos años deseábamos tener” y quiso agradecer “la colaboración e implicación de la Federación Canaria de Automovilismo y de los clubes relacionados con este deporte”.
Con este tipo de competiciones el municipio de Pájara se posiciona como uno de los puntos deportivos referentes en la isla y garantiza la puesta en marcha de una de las pruebas de motor más importantes a nivel regional.

noticias.titulo: Virginia de León continúa cuarta en la Copa Kobe Motor después del Rallye de Cáceres
noticias.texto:
Virginia de León continúa cuarta en la Copa Kobe Motor después del Rallye de Cáceres
Virginia de León y Fátima Toledo finalizan quintas en Cáceres antes de la última cita del campeonato
Balance positivo para Virginia de León tras su segunda incursión en el Rallye de Cáceres, que ha sido puntuable esta temporada para la Copa Kobe Motor. Un año y medio después de haber llegado como debutante a Extremadura, donde efectuó la primera de sus dos participaciones en el CERT (Campeonato de España de Rallyes de Tierra) 2025, la majorera ha regresado a los tramos cacereños, ahora ya al volante del Toyota Yaris Rally5 que está estrenando esta temporada.
La unidad con los colores de Ayuntamiento Puerto del Rosario – Proyecto Mujer y Motor, Vicepresidencia del Patronato de Turismo de Fuerteventura, FCA (Federación Canaria de Automovilismo) y Gobierno de Canarias y ha causado gran expectación en la ceremonia de salida de esta penúltima prueba puntuable para la monomarca de Kobe Motorsport 2026. Virginia de León y su copiloto, Fátima Toledo, las primeras mujeres canarias que desarrollan un programa deportivo de estas características a nivel nacional, han recibido una calurosa acogida por parte del público durante la ceremonia de inauguración, celebrada en la Plaza Mayor de Cáceres.
La piloto patrocinada asimismo por Adi, La Casa del Fontanero, Pastelería Panadería La Nueva Vicondesa, El Faro de Diego y Mojito Bar Fuerteventura ha mantenido la consistencia y fiabilidad que está demostrando a lo largo de su primera andadura con el Toyota Yaris Rally5 Kit de última generación.
Virginia de León y Fátima Toledo han evolucionado favorablemente por unos tramos con zonas muy veloces y estrechas, donde su confianza y ritmo de carrera se han ido incrementando cada vez más. En consecuencia, el dueto femenino de la Copa Kobe Motor ha ocupado la quinta posición final del Rallye de Cáceres; un resultado que mantiene a las canarias en cuarto lugar de la clasificación general antes de la última cita del calendario, el Rallye Ciudad de Granada (31 de octubre-1 de noviembre), donde las canarias podrán luchar por el podio definitivo del certamen promocional más consolidado del CERT (Campeonato de España de Rallyes de Tierra).
Virginia de León: "Los tramos del Rallye de Cáceres son muy rápidos y técnicos, por lo que hemos preferido ser más conservadoras esta vez. Tanto Fátima como yo nos encontramos cada vez mejor acopladas al Toyota Yaris Rally5 Kit. El público de Cáceres nos ha recibido con mucho cariño, hemos podido disfrutar de una prueba muy bonita, y aprovechar la experiencia para coger sensaciones con el coche en este tipo de terreno".

noticias.titulo: Otras noticias de interés
noticias.texto:
Álvaro Montoro: La nueva promesa argentina en Botafogo
En el universo del fútbol sudamericano, el nombre de Álvaro Montoro resuena con fuerza. Este mediocampista de apenas 18 años ha capturado la atención de aficionados exigentes, despertado el interés de gigantes europeos y convertido en pieza fundamental para Botafogo. Su historia es la de un chico de Tucumán que, con el balón pegado al pie, está escribiendo un capítulo dorado en su joven carrera.
¿Quién es Álvaro Montoro?
Datos personales y primeros años
Nacido el 17 de abril de 2007 en Concepción, Tucumán, Argentina, Álvaro Montoro llegó al mundo en una región donde el fútbol es religión. Con 170 centímetros de estatura y 65 kilogramos, este diestro natural desafía las estadísticas. Su cuerpo compacto se ha convertido en su mayor arma: un centro de gravedad bajo que le permite cambiar de dirección con agilidad felina Las casas de apuestas ajustaron sus cuotas cada vez que su nombre aparecía en las alineaciones, reconociendo el impacto instantáneo que este mediapunta podía generar en cualquier partido..Para los seguidores de apuestas online fútbol, Montoro se convirtió rápidamente en un nombre a seguir.
Origen y formación futbolística
La trayectoria de Álvaro Montoro comenzó en el Concepción Fútbol Club. A los 8 años, su familia se mudó a Buenos Aires. Primero recaló en Liniers, pero fue en 2017 cuando las puertas de La Fábrica de Vélez Sarsfield se abrieron para él.
? Hitos de formación:
- 2007: Nace en Concepción, Tucumán
- 2017: Ingresa a la academia de Vélez Sarsfield
- 2024: Debut profesional
- 2025: Salto al fútbol brasileño con Botafogo
Apodo y por qué es tan mediático
Lo bautizaron como "El Iniesta tucumano" por su capacidad para conducir el balón entre rivales. También se le conoce como "La Joya de Vélez". noticias.titulo: ¿Por qué acrygel uñas es la solución ideal para uñas débiles?
noticias.texto:
¿Por qué acrygel uñas es la solución ideal para uñas débiles?
¿Por qué acrygel uñas es la solución ideal para uñas débiles?
Las uñas débiles y quebradizas son uno de los problemas más comunes entre los clientes de la industria nail. El contacto constante con agua, los productos químicos domésticos e incluso el estrés pueden empeorar su estado. En estos casos, el esmalte tradicional a menudo no ofrece el resultado deseado. Por eso, cada vez más profesionales y clientes eligen acrygel uñas como una solución eficaz que combina fortalecimiento y estética.
Qué es acrygel uñas y cómo funciona
Acrygel uñas es un híbrido moderno de dos materiales: gel y acrílico. Combina las mejores propiedades de ambos: la resistencia del acrílico y la flexibilidad del gel. Gracias a su textura plástica, el material se modela fácilmente, permitiendo crear una forma natural de la uña sin volumen excesivo.
Su principal ventaja es su capacidad para fortalecer la placa ungueal sin sobrecargarla. Esto es especialmente importante para clientes con uñas finas y debilitadas.
Problemas principales de las uñas débiles
Para entender por qué acrygel uñas funciona, es importante prestar atención a los problemas típicos:
- Fragilidad y tendencia a astillarse incluso con mínima presión
- Deslaminación, que afecta no solo la apariencia sino también la estructura de la uña
- Excesiva finura, que hace que las uñas sean vulnerables
- Crecimiento lento, que impide alcanzar la longitud deseada
En estas condiciones, la manicura deja de ser solo estética. Las uñas necesitan una protección pensada, delicada pero eficaz, que no solo oculte el problema, sino que cree un entorno para su recuperación gradual.
¿Por qué el gel acrílico es la mejor opción?
Su versatilidad y fórmula pensada han convertido a este material en el favorito tanto de profesionales como de clientes que esperan un resultado perfecto sin compromisos.
- Fortalecimiento sin sobrecarga
El acrígel es mucho más ligero que el acrílico clásico, pero al mismo tiempo proporciona una base sólida. No crea sensación de “uñas pesadas” ni ejerce presión sobre la uña natural.
- Protección contra la fragilidad
El material forma una estructura resistente que protege las uñas de daños mecánicos. Gracias a esto, se reduce significativamente el riesgo de grietas y astilladuras.
- Apariencia natural
El acrígel permite crear un recubrimiento fino y cuidado, que se ve lo más natural posible. Es la opción ideal para quienes valoran la elegancia y el minimalismo.
- Comodidad al usarlo
A diferencia de muchos otros materiales, el acrígel casi no provoca molestias durante la polimerización. Su flexibilidad también ayuda a evitar lesiones en la uña.
En resumen, el acrígel no es solo una alternativa a otros materiales, sino una solución pensada que combina funcionalidad y estética, ofreciendo un resultado duradero y seguro.
Quién se beneficia especialmente del acrígel
Este material es la elección óptima para:
- Personas con uñas crónicamente débiles
- Clientes después de retirar extensiones
- Quienes tienen esmalte de gel que se descascarilla rápidamente
- Quienes desean dejar crecer la longitud natural de las uñas
Por eso, en los salones se recomienda a menudo el acrígel como solución básica para la recuperación de uñas.
Cuidado de las uñas con acrígel
Para mantener el resultado perfecto, es importante seguir algunas reglas simples:
- Hacer correcciones cada 2–3 semanas
- Usar aceite para cutículas regularmente
- Evitar cargas mecánicas fuertes
Este enfoque permite no solo conservar la estética de la manicura, sino también mejorar gradualmente el estado de las uñas naturales.
Conclusión
El acrígel no es solo una tendencia, sino una solución pensada para quienes enfrentan el problema de uñas débiles. Combina resistencia, comodidad y apariencia natural, ofreciendo un resultado duradero. Si buscas una manera de fortalecer tus uñas y al mismo tiempo lograr una manicura impecable, el acrígel es la elección óptima.

noticias.titulo: A lo concreto: ecotasa turística Por José Cabrera Noda
noticias.texto:
A lo concreto: ecotasa turística Por José Cabrera Noda
Secretario de Política Municipal, Sector Primario, Alimentación y Soberanía Alimentaria PSOE de Fuerteventura
Defiendo la implantación de una ecotasa turística como herramienta de financiación para la conservación ambiental y la mejora de la calidad de vida en Fuerteventura con criterios de sostenibilidad y concreción. No es un eslogan: es un planteamiento político concreto. Tan concreto como decir que debemos darle una solución permanente a la carretera entre Morro Jable y La Punta de Jandía. Veamos si ambos planteamientos concretos pueden confluir.
La ecotasa turística que defiendo para Fuerteventura no es una medida recaudatoria genérica, sino un instrumento finalista. Se recaudaría para financiar acciones concretas. No estoy inventando la pólvora, pero sí metiendo el dedo en un asunto que escuece a algunos sectores económicos de la isla. La ecotasa turística (que se aplica al visitante, no al residente) es un concepto ampliamente aplicado, conocido y aceptado en todo tipo de destinos europeos, por lo que el argumento de que como reacción vendrían menos turistas a la isla, afectando al empleo y la economía local, se desmonta por sí mismo.
El reto es hacer un uso inteligente de la medida y no implantarla por imitación de otros destinos. Si la futura ecotasa turística de Fuerteventura se dedica a acciones concretas de conservación ambiental y mejora de la calidad de vida de las personas que vivimos en la isla, bienvenida sea.
El ejemplo que se me viene a la cabeza es la carretera de La Punta de Jandía. Aquí hay un problema que debemos abordar con una solución estratégica y permanente. El sistema del recebe ya no es una solución. Cada vez es más complicado encontrar el material fino para igualar, rellenar los huecos y consolidar el firme de los 23 kilómetros de esta carretera. Y sacar ese árido del entorno de Jandía no parece lo más adecuado ni lo más sostenible desde los puntos de vista ambiental y paisajístico.
Ahí está el dilema que planteo para una de las vías más definitorias del ser majorero, de nuestra esencia, y también de nuestra imagen exterior. El sistema del recebe está alcanzando su final operativo y, con ello, mermará la seguridad en el tránsito de vehículos. Eso será otro problema añadido que se traducirá en accidentes de tráfico. Así que debemos encontrar otra solución y, en mi opinión, debe ser una solución permanente.
Para hacer realidad esa futura solución permanente para la carretera de La Punta de Jandía se necesita la confluencia de dos cosas: una solución técnica y jurídica que supere la actual etapa del tren de recebe y financiación para llevarla a término.
Para el primer condicionante se deberá congeniar el tránsito seguro de vehículos con las normas del Parque Natural de Jandía… otros muchos parques naturales tienen carreteras a las que se les ha dado una solución permanente. El segundo condicionante puede resolverse con una decisión política valiente y de largo recorrido: crear una ecotasa turística en Fuerteventura, de
naturaleza finalista, donde los majoreros y majoreras podamos decidir dónde invertir, en concreto, ese dinero. Para nuestro bienestar, para conservar nuestros paisajes, para empoderarnos en nuestro territorio. Una ecotasa turística para mejorar en lo concreto.

noticias.titulo: Puerto del Rosario recibe la primera visita del impresionante crucero Mein Schiff Relax
noticias.texto:
Puerto del Rosario recibe la primera visita del impresionante crucero Mein Schiff Relax
Dispone de 14 restaurantes y 17 bares, amplia zona de spa con 6 tipos de saunas gratuitas, terraza al aire libre y piscinas con vistas panorámicas
 Redacción NoticiasFuerteventura
Llega por primera vez a Puerto del Rosario el Crucero Mein Schiff Relax, un crucero de primer nivel mundial propulsado por gas licuado y referente en la navegación planetaria.
En la mañana de este jueves el alcalde, David de Vera, la concejala de Turismo, Rosa Rodríguez, la representación de la Autoridad Portuaria y la empresa consignataria, daban la bienvenida al crucero y fueron recibidos por el capitán Todd Burgmann y su equipo.
Por parte del ayuntamiento se obsequió al capitán con una cesta de productos típicos de la isla : queso, aceite, licor de leche de cabra, aloe vera, etc junto a algunas publicaciones del ayuntamiento, incluyendo el libreto de la exposición "The Canarian". El capitán hacía entrega de la tradicional metopa de esta nueva embarcación.
El Mein Schiff Relax es el primer crucero de la nueva clase "InTUItion" de la naviera alemana TUI Cruises, inaugurado en 2025.
Características principales:
* Tamaño y capacidad:
Mide aproximadamente 333 metros de eslora, cuenta con 19 cubiertas y puede albergar hasta 3.984 pasajeros y cerca de 1.400 tripulantes.
* Oferta gastronómica y de ocio:
Dispone de 14 restaurantes y 17 bares, una amplia zona de bienestar (spa) con 6 tipos de saunas gratuitas, terraza al aire libre, piscinas con vistas panorámicas y la Infinity Pool en la proa. Gimnasio 24 h. Pabellón cubierto y auditorio para 800 personas con actuaciones en directo, entre otros servicios.
* Sostenibilidad:
Funciona con un sistema de propulsión de gas natural licuado (GNL/LNG) y tecnologías avanzadas de eficiencia energética
En las encuestas de la propia empresa resaltan que en este destino aumenta la satisfacción de los clientes y el número de actividades que realizan en el exterior.

noticias.titulo: El Majorero Gabri tendrá su primera titularidad en Segunda División con el CD Tenerife
noticias.texto:
El Majorero Gabri tendrá su primera titularidad en Segunda División con el CD Tenerife
El guardameta majorero ocupará la portería del CD Tenerife ante el Ceuta por la sanción de Dani Martín y debutará como titular en la categoría
El guardameta majorero Gabri De Vuyst tendrá una oportunidad especial este domingo al estrenarse como titular en Segunda División con el CD Tenerife. El futbolista, nacido en Fuerteventura en 2004, ocupará la portería blanquiazul frente al Ceuta, en el encuentro que se disputará a las 12:00 horas en el Heliodoro Rodríguez López.
Su presencia en el once llega como consecuencia de la sanción de Dani Martín, expulsado en los últimos minutos del partido frente al Andorra. El portero asturiano vio dos tarjetas en el tramo final del encuentro, la segunda por lanzar el balón contra un adversario.
Para Gabri será su novena participación con el primer equipo del Tenerife. Hasta ahora ha disputado cinco encuentros en Primera RFEF, dos en la Copa del Rey y los últimos minutos del choque ante el Andorra, en el que encajó el gol del empate.
El majorero afronta así su primera gran oportunidad en el fútbol profesional. Su balance hasta el momento es de tres victorias, dos empates y tres derrotas, con seis goles encajados y cuatro partidos con la portería a cero.

noticias.titulo: Montero aboga por prohibir la vivienda vacacional en Canarias, donde el turismo se 'carga' la vida de los canarios
noticias.texto:
Montero aboga por prohibir la vivienda vacacional en Canarias, donde el turismo se 'carga' la vida de los canarios
Sobre inmigración, Montero defendió que no sobra ningún migrante y quiso citar al Evangelio: "Trata a los demás como te gustaría que te trataran a ti mismo"
La candidata de Podemos a la presidencia del Gobierno para las elecciones del 29 de noviembre, Irene Montero, ha abogado por prohibir la vivienda vacacional en Canarias y, además, ha acusado al turismo de estarse "cargando la vida misma" de los canarios.
La también eurodiputada pronunció estas palabras en un acto de campaña en la capital grancanaria ante unas 400 personas y junto a representantes de las otras formaciones con las que confluye en las islas: Nueva Canarias, Izquierda Unida y Sumar.
Sobre inmigración, Montero defendió que no sobra ningún migrante y quiso citar al Evangelio: "Trata a los demás como te gustaría que te trataran a ti mismo", aseveró, para a continuación reclamar la solidaridad de los territorios que, según ella, la derecha no quiere.
Así, abogó por no comprar más armas, por cargar con más impuestos a la banca y a las empresas, así como "a los ricos", para devolver el dinero "de arriba hacia abajo".
CULPA AL TURISMO DE PAGAR SUELDOS "MISERABLES"
"Que no cabemos todos es un bulo, además de que Canarias es un lugar de paso para muchos de ellos. Y en Adeje que hay un 30% de viviendas turísticas, ¿quién no cabe, una persona que necesita ayuda o el turismo desproporcionado que se está cargando la vida misma en Canarias", aseveró.
Si quieren recibir esta y toda la información GRATIS de Fuerteventura y Canarias puntualmente a través de nuestro canal de whatsApp, que no es un chat y no se puede enviar ni recibir comentarios, solamente información y videos de la isla, apuntarse al canal de Noticias Fuerteventura.
Además, culpó al turismo de pagar "salarios miserables", a las empresas de hacer negocio con todo, de contaminar y de "gastar más agua de la que se puede gastar".
Sostuvo que las familias no pueden vivir aquí con una renta media de 2.755 euros al mes y defendió que "Canarias tiene un límite, todo tiene un límite", por lo que "la economía de Canarias y la vida de los canarios no se puede organizar para los turistas".
ACUSA A PP Y VOX DE QUERER "LA ESCLAVITUD"
Montero dijo también que si fuera por PP y Vox habría "esclavitud, trabajo infantil" y "trabajo a destajo", que son el partido "de los señoritos" y de los "destajo arriba".
Defendió al pueblo palestino, un salario mínimo de 1.800 euros por 30 horas, porque la gente quiere "vivir": "Para eso hemos venido al mundo, para disfrutar, para vivir, para cuidar a nuestra gente" y concluyó reclamando "paz, casa y trabajo".

noticias.titulo: El verano acompañará todo noviembre en Fuerteventura
noticias.texto:
El verano acompañará todo noviembre en Fuerteventura
Vientos flojos del este, y temperaturas sobre los 25 grados, nos acompañan durante todo el mes
 Redacción NoticiasFuerteventura
El otoño sigue siendo verano en la isla de Fuerteventura, al menos en cuanto a las temperaturas. Tras el paso de varias borrascas atlánticas que no han dejado grandes acumulados en la isla, todos los modelos apuntan a una segunda quincena de noviembre con tiempo anticiclónico y temperaturas veraniegas.
Vientos flojos de nor-noreste, cielos despejados la mayor parte del día y el mercurio por encima de 25 grados en muchas zonas del interior y del sur serán la tónica, al menos hasta fin de mes.
Si quieren recibir esta y toda la información GRATIS de Fuerteventura y Canarias puntualmente a través de nuestro canal de whatsApp, que no es un chat y no se puede enviar ni recibir comentarios, solamente información y videos de la isla, apuntarse al canal de Noticias Fuerteventura.
Todos los modelos apuntan a que tendremos un mes de noviembre más cálido de lo normal, en un año que está resultando especialmente cálido por el fenómeno climático El Niño, que está modulando todo el clima planetario.
Aguas más calientes en todo el litoral majorero y con el mar en relativa calma, olas que pueden llegar a 1.5 metros pero que subirán con fuerza a partir del miércoles de esta semana entrante. Se recomienda precaución en el baño en toda Fuerteventura, pero especialmente al norte y oeste de la isla.

noticias.titulo: This is a remarkable diplomatic moment for China's Xi - but it comes with pitfalls
noticias.resumen: The meeting comes with challenges as there are things Xi does not appear keen to discuss with Putin and Trump.
noticias.texto:
This is a remarkable diplomatic moment for China's Xi - but it comes with pitfalls
- Published
Xi Jinping will believe he has achieved something no other world leader could in securing a historic summit with Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump in Shenzhen.
For decades, Washington and its western allies shaped the world order.
Yet it is China that has orchestrated the remarkable diplomatic spectacle of three of the world's most powerful protagonists sitting around the table.
And surrounding it all is the futuristic display that is Shenzhen, with driverless cars cruising past as drones fly overhead and robots - literally - dance in the streets.
Ostensibly, this is an economic summit for Asia Pacific leaders. But for Xi, it is also a demonstration of China's grip on the global economy and world politics.
His country is no longer just reacting to decisions made in Washington, London or Brussels - instead Beijing is at the heart of conversations which are reshaping the international order.
But this meeting is not without its pitfalls for Xi as there are many things he does not appear keen to discuss with Putin and Trump.
Ukraine, the balancing act
First, China is not keen for the war in Ukraine, now well into its fifth year, to be on the agenda.
This is a delicate balancing act for Xi who is aware his relationship with Putin may damage China's connections in Europe. The EU is a key market, especially now when the Chinese economy is heavily relying on exports.
However Xi also doesn't want the war to end in a way that will destabilise Russia, a key ally and neighbour.
Beijing is still trying to maintain that it is neutral in this war and has repeatedly called for negotiations and a political settlement while avoiding condemnation of Russia's full-scale invasion.
The US, especially under the previous Biden administration, and Europe have accused China of sending Russia components that it could use in its war in Ukraine, while also propping up the country's economy by buying oil and gas.
Xi wants to keep Putin close, but not too close because he also doesn't want Russia's problems to become China's problems.
China's growing nuclear arsenal
Donald Trump has already made it clear he wants the three leaders to discuss limiting the world's supply of nuclear weapons.
The US and Russia possess the world's largest stockpile of nuclear warheads. But China is rapidly expanding its own arsenal, which is raising alarm bells in Washington.
The last major US-Russian arms control treaty, known as New START, expired in February this year, triggering fears of an arms race. The agreement had set a cap to control the number of nuclear weapons in US and Russia's arsenal.
Trump would like China to be included in any new agreement, but Beijing has pushed back.
Xi's argument will be that his arsenal is considerably smaller than what Washington and Moscow own, and, therefore, it would be unfair for Beijing to be bound by their limits. China also believes it should have the freedom to develop its own nuclear capabilities.
This subject could complicate Xi's bid for China to be recognised as a leader on the world stage - because the US could argue that the status includes being a responsible nuclear power.
Will everyone stick to the script?
Xi will want to control the optics of this meeting, from start to finish.
Chinese officials like to nail down agendas with talking points and produce carefully choreographed speeches.
But in this unprecedented summit, Xi will have to live with two very unpredictable leaders.
Both Trump and Putin have their own agendas and the US President has already threatened to go off script.
There is a risk that they both dominate the meeting and Xi ends up looking like a host, rather than the architect of a major diplomatic moment.
Of course, Xi may be ready for this. It may even play into his hands.
The Chinese leader has been trying to portray himself as a stable global leader - at this summit he will be flanked by two men embroiled in wars they cannot seem to end.
So any unscripted moment could serve to highlight his preferred role as senior statesman.
Xi's problems at home
For all the attention, this meeting of three men with vastly different agendas is unlikely to yield any significant outcomes.
But the power it projects is important for Xi as he heads towards next year's Communist Party Congress, where he is expected to secure a historic fourth term as leader of the party and country.
He may hope to use this as propaganda at home, given the country is grappling with huge domestic challenges.
A country-wide property crisis has dented consumer confidence. Local governments are heavily in debt. Manufacturing has slowed and more of China's workforce has become dependent on flexible jobs with no pension or social security. One in five young people are thought to be struggling to find work. Frustration and anxiety about the future bubble up routinely.
Xi does not have to deal with elections, and the country has not seen major protests in decades. But he will be concerned about his popularity within the party elite as these problems - and the palpable frustrations they produce - grow.
At a time like this, a photo-op with Putin and Trump may offer him proof that his country's "century of humiliation" is over. China is no longer a rising power, he can argue - rather, it is increasingly shaping the rules of a new era.

noticias.titulo: Dozens missing after boat carrying 100 migrants sinks off Senegal's coast
noticias.resumen: Some local media report that at least four bodies have been recovered.
noticias.texto:
Dozens missing after boat carrying 100 migrants sinks off Senegal's coast
- Published
Senegalese authorities are continuing search operations after a boat reportedly carrying about 100 migrants capsized off the coast.
Initial reports said that one person had died, but some local media have reported that at least four bodies have been recovered. Dozens of people are still missing.
Personal belongings were found on the badly damaged boat, which washed ashore near the village of Yenne, south of Dakar. Search operations continued throughout Wednesday and were due to resume on Thursday.
This comes less than two weeks after a shipwreck off the coast of the north-western town of Thieppe killed at least 39 people, in one of Senegal's deadliest migration disasters.
Oumar Sow, a representative of the village chief, said the latest tragedy happened around 02:00 local time (02:00 GMT).
"Cries could be heard coming from the pirogue that were audible even from the beach," the AFP news agency quoted him as saying.
A survivor questioned by the police said there were about 100 people on the boat, including five women, AFP reported.
Police recovered identity documents, several mobile phones and personal belongings from the wreckage, including a school enrolment document.
At a cabinet meeting on Wednesday, President Diomaye Faye expressed concern about a renewed increase in irregular departure by migrants hoping to reach Europe.
He instructed the interior ministry to prepare a report examining the factors driving the dangerous journeys and proposing measures to tackle the problem.
Following last month's tragedy, Faye had urged Senegalese people not to risk their lives attempting the dangerous sea crossings.
Many thousands of people from West Africa have died or gone missing trying to flee conflict, authoritarian rule or poverty in recent years.
The UN's migration agency IOM said last month that it had recorded at least 454 deaths and disappearances off the West African coast this year alone.
It warned the figures were likely to be an underestimate, as many boats disappear without leaving survivors or a trace.
As it has become more difficult to reach Europe through North Africa, due to tighter controls and increased co-operation with European countries, migrants are increasingly targeting Spain's Canary Islands.
They often travel in wooden boats known as pirogues that are frequently overloaded and not suited to such long voyages across the Atlantic Ocean.
Most migrants arriving in the Canary Islands this year are from Senegal, according to the UN.
They are driven to leave home by limited employment opportunities, family pressures and established migration networks, according to the IOM.
On 7 November, El Hierro, one of the Canary Islands, declared a state of emergency following a surge in migrant arrivals.
It said more than 3,300 people had reached the island in about 30 boats since the beginning of the month. This amounts to almost a third of the island's population.

noticias.titulo: Survivors of Uganda's deadly landslide seek justice at the UN
noticias.resumen: Survivors reject relocation plans they say ignore their safety, land rights and livelihoods
noticias.texto:
Survivors of Uganda's deadly landslide seek justice at the UN
- Published
Survivors of a 2019 landslide in eastern Uganda that killed more than 50 people have taken their fight for relocation and compensation to the United Nations.
The 48 complainants accuse the government of violating Uganda's constitution by failing to put effective disaster management measures in Bududa, a mountainous district prone to landslides.
Their case comes as heavy rains raise the risk of further landslides. They say the government relocation programme ignores their safety, land rights and livelihoods.
The UN Human Rights Committee is considering what is believed to be the first case seeking climate adaptation measures, one that could set a global precedent.
At least 33 of the 53 people who died in the 2019 landslide were children. Years later, survivors say every spell of heavy rain brings back fears of another tragedy.
William Tsama, one of the claimants, lost four members of his family.
"My quest should be a lesson," he said.
"Victims in such situations, ignored by governments, can take them to court to compel them to help their citizens."
Uganda introduced a resettlement plan for landslide-prone areas in 2011, but progress has been limited, with relatively few people relocated.
Last month, it launched a new resettlement programme offering affected households 18m Ugandan shillings ($4,300; Â£3,300) to help them move to safer areas.
But some survivors have questioned whether the amount is enough to cover the cost of relocating and rebuilding their lives.
Under the programme, families can choose between receiving two acres of land, valued at 8m shillings, plus 10m shillings towards building a house, or taking the equivalent land allowance in cash, alongside the same housing grant.
The scheme is expected to benefit 1,410 households identified as living in high-risk areas.
The government has now given residents of designated high-risk areas two months, from November to December, to leave or face forced eviction.
The threat extends beyond landslides. The complainants say changing rainfall patterns and declining soil fertility have also affected farming, leaving many families struggling to secure their livelihoods.
"I want to get a new good place for my people, so even if I die, they will be okay. I am an old man, but I am doing it for my children," Tsama said.
The survivors first launched legal action in 2020 in Uganda, and received support from Ugandan environmental organisation Greenwatch three years later.
They are seeking compensation for lost family members and livelihoods, as well as emergency measures, including accessible early-warning systems in high-risk areas.
Greenwatch Executive Director Samantha Atukunda Kakuru Mwesigwa said the case is about changing how governments prepare and respond to climate-related disasters.
"Justice for claimants is not just about winning in court. It is about forcing government policy to keep pace with a changing climate, and ensuring loss and damage is no longer an afterthought in disaster management," she said.
The threat of climate-related disasters extends across East Africa.
In Kenya, floods and landslides killed at least 181 people between March and May 2024, according to the Kenya Red Cross. In Rwanda, floods and landslides killed 135 people in May 2023.
The dangers are also being felt further afield. In October 2026, a flash flood swept through Nepal's Gorkha district after a landslide blocked a river, washing away homes and infrastructure, and killing over 1,500 people.
"Disasters like the one in Bududa are only getting worse because of climate change â and they are happening all around the world, as we've seen recently and tragically in Nepal," ClientEarth lawyer Vesselina Newman said.
She said poorer countries, which have contributed relatively little to global emissions, are bearing some of the heaviest consequences of climate change and need greater financial support.
"High income countries must provide financial assistance and ensure that sufficient money goes directly to countries like Uganda, so they can roll out life-saving adaptation measures," she said.
The complainants say relocation must involve more than moving people out of danger.
They want the government to protect their livelihoods, respect their land rights, and take account of individual needs.
The case is now before the United Nations Human Rights Committee, which will ask the Ugandan government to respond within six months.

noticias.titulo: 'It's a dream come true' – South African DJ celebrates featuring in GTA 6
noticias.resumen: Several African stars feature
noticias.texto:
'It's a dream come true' â South African DJ celebrates featuring in GTA 6
- Published
South African DJ Lag says it is a "dream come true" to have his music featured on Grand Theft Auto 6 (GTA 6), the hugely popular video game released on Thursday.
DJ lag, one of South Africa's best-known electronic music producers, is among several African stars to feature, alongside Nigerian singers Burna Boy and Asake.
"I can't explain the feeling. I started playing the game last night and it's amazing," DJ Lag told the BBC's Newsday programme, adding that he had been playing GTA since he was about 10 years old and could hardly believe he was now part of the latest edition.
Many players have already had a chance to play the game following its worldwide launch.
The game, which lets players explore a fictional American city, features a dedicated African music radio station playing Afrobeats, amapiano and other sounds from across the continent.
The release of GTA 6 ends a 13-year wait for a new edition of the game.
Rockstar Games, the developer behind the franchise, has revealed details of the game's soundtrack and some in-game radio stations, but has yet to release a complete list of songs featured in the game.
Rockstar says AfroBank FM features everything from 20th Century African classics to contemporary amapiano and 3-step, giving the continent's music a prominent place in the latest edition.
Burna Boy co-hosts the station alongside British DJ and producer Palms Trax, while Asake's hit song Joha is among the tracks players can listen to as they drive around the game's virtual world.
DJ Lag, whose real name is Lwazi Asanda Gwala, is regarded as one of the pioneers of gqom, a genre of electronic dance music that emerged in the port city of Durban in the early 2010s.
He posted on Instagram: "God did."
Ghanaian highlife legends Pat Thomas and Ebo Taylor also feature, alongside South African artists Robot Boii and Kamo Mphela, bringing a mix of classic and contemporary African music to one of gaming's biggest franchises.
Rockstar has also announced a 34-track official soundtrack album, released in partnership with Atlantic Records, featuring an original Burna Boy song titled Bigger.
For African fans, the inclusion of familiar music adds another dimension to the experience, allowing players to hear some of the continent's biggest sounds while exploring the American setting.
The series allows players to roam through sprawling fictional cities, drive vehicles and complete missions involving crime, police pursuits and other adventures.
The latest instalment takes players to Vice City, a fictional version of Miami, and the surrounding US state of Leonida, inspired by Florida.
Its story follows two criminals, Jason and Lucia, who become caught up in a wider conspiracy after a robbery goes wrong.
The launch has generated enormous excitement among gamers around the world.
Some fans downloaded it in advance so they could begin playing as soon as it became available, while others have booked leave from work.
The previous edition, GTA 5, was one of the best-selling video games of all time, selling more than 200 million copies worldwide.
The new release is expected to be another major commercial success, although it remains to be seen whether it will match its predecessor's extraordinary sales.

noticias.titulo: Denmark parliament approves security deal with Greenland and US
noticias.resumen: All 109 Danish lawmakers present approved the deal, easing tensions over Trump's desire to annex the Arctic island.
noticias.texto:
Denmark parliament approves security deal with Greenland and US
All 109 Danish lawmakers present approved the deal, easing tensions over Trump’s desire to annex the Arctic island.
The Danish parliament has unanimously ratified a security agreement with the United States covering Greenland, aimed at bolstering security in the Arctic and North Atlantic.
Thursday’s decision to approve the deal signed in September eases tensions over US President Donald Trump’s desire to annex the Arctic island.
In the 179-seat parliament, known as the Folketing, the 109 members present voted in favour of the text, which was adopted without opposition or abstention.
The vote, which followed the second reading of the text, went through without any debate or opposition.
In early November, Greenland’s parliament had passed it by 16 votes, with seven abstentions.
The US, Denmark and Greenland signed the agreement in September to resolve tensions after Trump repeatedly threatened to take control of the mineral-rich island, a self-governing Danish territory home to 57,000 people.
The deal is not subject to a vote by the US Senate. The executive agreement, following Thursday’s vote in Copenhagen, will enter into force once the Danish Ministry of Foreign Affairs informs the US in a diplomatic note that procedures are complete.
Signed in New York on September 22, the agreement supplements a 1951 accord on the US military presence in Greenland.
It allows the US to build two military bases in Greenland and blocks countries outside the European Union and NATO from strategic sectors, in order to stop China or Russia from gaining influence over the territory, particularly through investments.
Greenland is an autonomous territory of Denmark, but the deal is to remain in force even if Greenland gains full independence.
Since returning to the presidency in January 2025, Trump has repeatedly insisted that the US needed to control Greenland for strategic reasons, alarming NATO ally Denmark and other partners.
The shortest route from Europe to North America runs via strategically located Greenland, where the northernmost US military base is located.

noticias.titulo: FIFA confirms Diallo, Tashima as Infantino’s challengers at 2027 election
noticias.resumen: French football chief Philippe Diallo and Japan's Kozo Tashima will be the only candidates to run for FIFA presidency.
noticias.texto:
FIFA confirms Diallo, Tashima as Infantino’s challengers at 2027 election
French football chief Philippe Diallo and Japan’s Kozo Tashima will be the only candidates to run for FIFA presidency next March when Infantino seeks re-election.
FIFA president Gianni Infantino’s re-election bid will be challenged by the French and Japanese federations’ presidents, Philippe Diallo and Kozo Tashima, football’s global governing body has confirmed.
Former Swiss defender Ramon Vega, who announced his intention to run last month, was not among the candidates FIFA mentioned on Thursday.
The election, set to be held in March 2027, will be the first time Infantino faces a challenger after being re-elected without opposition in 2023.
French Football Federation (FFF) president Diallo announced his candidacy on Monday, with the support of UEFA member associations represented on the executive committee and the FIFA Council.
Tashima, the Japanese Federation’s Association president, declared his bid earlier this month and formally submitted his nomination on Wednesday.
“The candidatures have been forwarded to the electoral committee for examination and for passing a decision on the admission of the candidates,” FIFA said in a statement.
“Member associations will be notified of the names of the proposed and admitted candidates no later than 18 February 2027.”
Infantino has faced repeated calls for his resignation since his FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, a bid to sell stakes in the World Cup and other major competitions, failed.
But the 56-year-old Swiss native, who has been the FIFA president since 2016, maintains that he has enough support from member associations around the world to get him re-elected.
Diallo, who took over as FFF president in 2023, played a leading role as France and other European associations withdrew their support from Infantino this year over the FFE controversy.
“Against the backdrop of serious concerns over the direction of FIFA, the national associations called for renewed unity and trust within the global football community,” UEFA said on Monday.

noticias.titulo: UN top court convicts Myanmar of ‘genocidal intent’ against Rohingya
noticias.resumen: In case filed at the ICJ in 2019, The Gambia accused Myanmar of breaching the 1948 Genocide Convention.
noticias.texto:
UN top court convicts Myanmar of ‘genocidal intent’ against Rohingya
In case filed at the ICJ in 2019, The Gambia accused Myanmar of breaching the 1948 Genocide Convention.
The United Nations’s top court has found Myanmar guilty of “genocidal intent” in massacres that killed 10,000 Rohingya in its military operations in 2017.
The International Court of Justice (ICJ) at The Hague delivered its judgement on Thursday over the military crackdown that drove more than 730,000 mainly Muslim Rohingya to flee to neighbouring Bangladesh.
Evidence shows Myanmar forces killed some 10,000 Rohingya, ICJ President Yuji Iwasawa said during a three-hour readout of the verdict.
“The Court finds that Myanmar’s security forces killed thousands of Rohingya civilians, perpetrated widespread acts of sexual violence as well as acts of extreme violence against children and attacked fleeing Rohingya as they sought to flee in large numbers to Bangladesh,” he added.
In specific cases that he referred to, he said Myanmar had acted with “genocidal intent”.
The case was brought by the West African nation of The Gambia, which in 2019 accused Myanmar of seeking to destroy the Rohingya people. It asked the ICJ to rule that Myanmar has breached the 1948 Genocide Convention, order the nation to put an end to any illegal activities targeting the Rohingya and ensure those responsible for genocide are punished.
Myanmar, meanwhile, has claimed its crackdown was in response to attacks by fighters from the Arakan Rohingya Salvation Army (ARSA) on police posts.
The ICJ said that the “only reasonable inference” from evidence of widespread atrocities by Myanmar security forces is that they had the intent to destroy a “substantial part” of the Rohingya minority.
It said Myanmar should have known that there was a risk of genocide when armed civilians participated in the military campaign. “Myanmar thus violated its obligation to prevent genocide,” it added.
More than 1.3 million Rohingya remain displaced across South and Southeast Asia, including 1.2 million in sprawling refugee camps in Cox’s Bazar in Bangladesh, according to the United Nations.
Conflict, shrinking humanitarian aid and dangerous sea crossings continue to leave many members of the community displaced and vulnerable.
More to come…

noticias.titulo: ‘Displacement by design’: Trump’s Gaza peace plan a failure, aid groups say
noticias.resumen: With two million Palestinians confined to an area of less than 130sq km, UN-backed Gaza peace plan has collapsed.
noticias.texto:
‘Displacement by design’: Trump’s Gaza peace plan a failure, aid groups say
A year after the UN-backed ceasefire, 2 million Palestinians are confined to an area of less than 130sq km as Israeli territorial expansion and aid blockades deepen the crisis.
One year after the United Nations Security Council endorsed the Trump administration’s 20-point Comprehensive Plan to end the Gaza Conflict, a coalition of five prominent international aid organisations has issued a damning assessment.
As Israeli forces launched a new ground offensive in central Gaza this week, advancing with tanks west of its “Yellow Line”, and issued new forced evacuation orders, in violation of the peace plan, the Danish Refugee Council, Norwegian Refugee Council, Oxfam, Refugees International and Save the Children, released a humanitarian scorecard which grades the plan at just four out of 26 possible points. The plan scored a zero on humanitarian access and earned just one point for civilian protection.
Israel’s expanding military footprint
Despite the Gaza Peace Plan’s explicit prohibition against territorial occupation in Gaza – and its requirement that Israeli forces withdraw – the Israeli military “Yellow Line” has moved further west, expanding control of Gaza territory from 58 percent at the start of the ceasefire 13 months ago, to 65 percent today, according to OCHA. Israel itself has said it controls 70 percent of the territory, a UN official told the UN Security Council in June this year.
Palestinians are not allowed to cross the line, so this expansion has confined roughly 2.1 million Palestinians to just 128sq km (49 sq miles), according to OCHA last month, squeezing 16,000 people into each square km. More recent analysis suggests it may be even smaller. Recent map analysis by US news group NPR found the confinement area is now just 109sq km (42 sq miles), creating a population density of nearly 19,300 people per sq km.
Ramy Abdu, founder and chairman of the Euro-Mediterranean Human Rights Monitor, warned that Israel is carrying out unlawful acquisition of territory by force.
The human cost has been devastating, agencies say, with at least 1,650 Palestinians killed and 5,975 wounded since the “ceasefire” was declared in October last year.
Earlier this week, Shaun Hughes, World Food Programme (WFP) country director for Palestine, told journalists: “When you’re in Gaza, it does not feel like a ceasefire. Israeli military control across nearly 70 per cent of Gaza means that people have almost no space to grow their own food. Fishing in the sea is prohibited and also life-threatening. Unemployment is over 80 per cent, so without humanitarian assistance, people have little or no alternate means of survival.”
Lilu Thapa, executive director for the Middle East, Asia and Europe at the Danish Refugee Council, said: “Palestinians in Gaza are being confined as the “Yellow Line” expands. This is displacement by design, and a ceasefire that allows it is a ceasefire in name only.”
A ‘political shield’ for genocide
The diplomatic framework overseeing this crisis, specifically the Board of Peace and International Stabilization Force (ISF) established by United States President Donald Trump, has drawn intense scrutiny from human rights experts who accuse the body of abandoning its mandate.
“Euro-Med Human Rights Monitor believes that, from the moment of its establishment, the Board of Peace represented a serious infringement on the Palestinian people’s right to self-determination, both in its composition and in the powers entrusted to it,” Abdu told Al Jazeera.
The Board, chaired by the US, operates without any meaningful Palestinian representation, Abdu said.
“Instead, it has effectively become a political shield for Israel’s occupation and its crimes, contributing to the perpetuation of genocidal conditions while providing political cover for grave violations of international law,” Abdu told Al Jazeera. “The available evidence supports describing the Board’s role as a form of functional normalisation of genocide and starvation.”
Mohsen Abu Ramadan, a board member of the Palestinian NGOs Network, said: “Regretfully, the Board of Peace failed the international community and continues to provide political cover for ongoing genocide and atrocities.”
Aid blockade deepens
The peace plan announced last year stipulated that a minimum of 600 UN-coordinated humanitarian aid trucks would be allowed to enter Gaza daily. In reality, an average of just 49 UN-coordinated trucks entered the Strip each day in September.
Only two percent of these limited convoys carried medical supplies, leading to critical shortages and deaths from treatable illnesses.
Instead, Israeli authorities have increasingly prioritised the entry of commercial trucks carrying expensive goods that the impoverished population cannot afford to buy.
During the week of October 12, of 315 commercial trucks which entered Gaza, 223 carried food and 51 carried non-essential items. Only 12 carried hygiene and shelter materials and just a single truck carried medical supplies.
Israel has cited “dual use” restrictions, which restrict the entry of products and goods which have a military as well as a civilian purpose.
Jan Egeland, CEO of the Norwegian Refugee Council, said that the crisis stems from political decisions. “The suffering of Gaza’s 2.1 million people is not inevitable. The world must stop accepting it,” Egeland said. Oxfam America President Abby Maxman noted that the reality on the ground is a “direct result of policy choices made in Israel, the US and at the UN.”
Mounting winter crisis
As Gaza enters its fourth winter of displacement, the shelter crisis has reached breaking point.
While donors have pledged about $18bn for Gaza via the Board of Peace, more than a year after the ceasefire was declared, reconstruction has yet to begin and nearly 1.4m Palestinians are living in makeshift shelters.
A recent winter storm flooded more than 70,000 tents in a single day, resulting in the drowning of an infant and the deaths of five displaced people. While stocks of tents and blankets inside Gaza are virtually exhausted, more than 150,000 tents and 500,000 blankets are locked outside the territory’s borders, waiting for permission to enter.
“What greater moral and legal outrage could there be than invoking so-called dual-use restrictions to prevent the entry of tents and basic hygiene supplies as winter approaches?” Abdu told Al Jazeera.
Save the Children International CEO Inger Ashing said: “One year ago, the world was promised that Gaza’s children would finally see safety, relief and a chance to rebuild their lives. Instead, they are colder, hungrier, more traumatised and more at risk than they were before.”
Jeremy Konyndyk, president of Refugees International, called on international backers to act. “The United States and other UN Security Council members must use their leverage to ensure those obligations are met,” he said.
Legal accountability
With the medical evacuation system collapsing, Gaza’s health ministry has reported that 2,027 patients have died while awaiting transfer and 21,000 remain on waiting lists.
Abdu outlined five complementary paths towards accountability, including the enforcement of International Criminal Court (ICC) arrest warrants for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and other officials, the continuation of International Court of Justice (ICJ) genocide proceedings against Israel and the pursuit of universal jurisdiction in national courts. He also called for regional arms embargoes on Israel and pressed the UN Security Council to hold a public briefing to examine the Board of Peace’s failures.
“No institution, regardless of its name, mandate or political sponsorship, can legitimately claim to be advancing peace while allowing the killing of civilians, the destruction of the conditions necessary for human survival and the expansion of an unlawful occupation to continue unchecked,” Abdu told Al Jazeera.
Board blames Israeli ‘political indecision’
Al Jazeera contacted the Board of Peace for a response to these claims. In response, head of communications Brad Klapper sent us the Board’s latest official report via WhatsApp. He did not address the specific allegations about encroachment on territory or refusal of permission for aid trucks to enter the enclave.
When pressed by Al Jazeera for direct answers to these inquiries, Klapper stated: “This is your reply. You have our assessment of where things stand.”
The report provided by Klapper included an acknowledgement of the failures to implement the peace plan in Gaza but appeared to place the blame on Israeli political indecision in several areas.
“…Implementation on the ground, however, has been limited, pending decisions that need to be taken by the parties… as soon as the necessary decisions are adopted by the Government of Israel,” the report states in one part.
Later, it also states: “The absence of decisions by the Government of Israel on the necessary conditions and arrangements for the training, deployment and return of civilian police to Gaza continues to impede full implementation of the Comprehensive Plan.”
Paragraph 49 of the report states: “That process, which relies not on trust but on verified results, cannot begin while the requisite decisions remain pending. The Board of Peace therefore urges Israel… to take without delay the decisions required for the training, deployment and return of the civilian police and for the entry of the NCAG and the ISF”, referring to National Committee for the Administration of Gaza (NCAG) and the International Stabilization Force (ISF) which are provided for under the peace plan, but which have yet to be allowed to enter Gaza.
The report also highlights that Hamas and Palestinian factions accepted a 15-point roadmap on July 30 to relinquish their weapons and transfer full authority to a transitional administration.
However, it notes that execution mechanisms for this remain paralysed and states that the absence of decisions by the Israeli government continues to impede the plan.
Concluding its report, the Board states in the report: “A ceasefire that delivers nothing visible cannot be sustained indefinitely. The people of Gaza have paid the highest price for this war and should not be asked to pay again for delay.”

noticias.titulo: Malaysian weightlifting champion Roslin loses arm after motorbike crash
noticias.resumen: Muhammad Hafizuddin Roslin, who won a gold medal at the Commonwealth Games 2026, had his arm amputated after accident.
noticias.texto:
Malaysian weightlifting champion Roslin loses arm after motorbike crash
Muhammad Hafizuddin Roslin, who won a gold medal at the Commonwealth Games 2026, had his arm amputated after an accident.
Malaysia’s Commonwealth Games gold medal-winning weightlifter Muhammad Hafizuddin Roslin had his right arm amputated after a motorcycle accident but is in a stable condition in hospital, a Malaysian sports official said.
Roslin was “awake and smiling,” following a seven-hour-long surgery at Kuala Lumpur Hospital, Malaysia Weightlifting Federation president Ayub Rahmat told the AFP news agency on Thursday.
The 21-year-old was conscious and in a stable condition in hospital, three days after the crash, the country’s top weightlifting official said.
Roslin reportedly lost control of his motorcycle while riding on the expressway on Monday night and sustained injuries to his right leg and arm, a haematoma – pooled blood – in the neck, as well as minor head injuries, according to Malaysian media.
Doctors amputated Hafizuddin’s arm above the elbow, local media reports said.
“Physically, his condition is improving but this incident has had a great impact on his future,” Rahmat said. He called it “a shock and a huge loss” for weightlifting in the country.
The Malaysian government said it would cover all treatment costs.
“The government, through the [National Sports Council], is fully covering the costs of treatment and medical care related to the incident, including follow-up treatment and hospital accommodation until he is discharged,” the ministry said in a statement on Wednesday.
It added that Roslin’s training allowance would also continue at the current eligible rate.
Malaysian’s Sultan Idris Education University (UPSI) also offered psychological support and sports psychology intervention for Roslin as part of his recovery, Malaysian media reported.
“In this critical situation, an athlete’s greatest challenge is not merely the physical healing process, but also how to cope with emotional shock, the denial phase and the sudden loss of sporting identity,” said Dr Jaffry Zakaria, associate professor of the Faculty of Sports Science and Coaching (FSSK) at UPSI.
Hafizuddin won gold at this year’s Commonwealth Games in the men’s 88kg category and set a games record with a total lift of 345kg. His attempt of 162kg in the snatch category set a national record as well as a games record.
He was a prospect for the country at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympics.

noticias.titulo: North Korea expanding uranium enrichment facility, UN nuclear watchdog says
noticias.resumen: North Korea can produce both highly enriched uranium and weapons-grade plutonium at its facilities, according to IAEA.
noticias.texto:
North Korea expanding uranium enrichment facility, UN nuclear watchdog says
North Korea can produce both highly enriched uranium and weapons-grade plutonium at its facilities, according to the IAEA.
North Korea is expanding a nuclear facility for enriching uranium, according to the head of the United Nations nuclear watchdog, the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA).
An existing facility at the Yongbyon nuclear centre has been further expanded in the last couple of months, IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi said on Wednesday.
This comes as US President Donald Trump expressed his eagerness to meet North Korean leader Kim Jong Un while he is in Asia for an APEC leaders’ summit in China.
“Since mid-September 2026, a further extension to the original Yongbyon enrichment facility has been under construction with the new extension externally complete by late October 2026,” Grossi said in a statement to the IAEA’s board of governors.
“The ongoing expansion of the DPRK’s uranium enrichment program remains extremely worrying,” he added, using North Korea’s official name, the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea.
Pyongyang has not allowed IAEA inspectors into the country for years. The IAEA, nevertheless, keeps watch on North Korea’s nuclear facilities, including through satellite imagery and open-source information.
North Korea has called its Yongbyon complex “the heart” of its nuclear programme. Nuclear weapons can be built using either highly enriched uranium or weapons-grade plutonium, and North Korea has facilities to produce both at Yongbyon.
North Korean Foreign Minister Choe Son Hui last week stressed that possessing such weapons was “the strongest guarantee” of his country’s sovereignty. Choe rejected the recent demand for North Korea’s complete nuclear disarmament by the Group of Seven (G7) economically powerful democracies.
Disarmament of the global nuclear weapons arsenal is likely to be a topic at the trilateral meeting between Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on Thursday in Shenzhen, at Trump’s request.
While Trump expressed interest in meeting with Kim, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio later said no meeting was yet scheduled with the North Korean leader during Trump’s Asia visit. However, he added that the president is prepared to begin a new dialogue with Pyongyang.

noticias.titulo: Kenya’s marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir gets three-year ban for doping
noticias.resumen: Jepchirchir breached anti-doping rules by testing positive for banned substance EPO, Athletics Integrity Unit says.
noticias.texto:
Kenya’s marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir gets three-year ban for doping
Jepchirchir admitted to breaching anti-doping rules relating to the presence of banned substance EPO, Athletics Integrity Unit says.
Kenya’s reigning world and former Olympic marathon champion Peres Jepchirchir has been suspended for three years after testing positive for the banned substance EPO, the Athletics Integrity Unit (AIU) said.
Jepchirchir admitted to breaching anti-doping rules relating to the presence of a prohibited substance or its metabolites and to the use or attempted use of a prohibited substance or prohibited method, the AIU said in a statement on Thursday.
EPO, a synthetic form of erythropoietin, is a laboratory-made version of a natural hormone produced mainly by the kidneys that signals the bone marrow to make more red blood cells, according to the Mayo Clinic.
Athletes sometimes misuse synthetic EPO as a performance-enhancing drug to boost oxygen delivery to muscles and improve endurance.
Jepchirchir was provisionally suspended last month after the AIU, which investigates doping in track and field athletes on behalf of the sport’s governing body, World Athletics, returned an adverse analytical finding for EPO from an out-of-competition sample collected in Kenya before her Sydney Marathon victory in late August.
Jepchirchir has accepted the disqualification of all of her competitive results since July 17.
The 33-year-old won women’s marathon gold at the Tokyo Olympics in 2021 and the world title last year. She is also a former world record holder in the half marathon.
The Sydney Marathon, which noted that Jepchirchir’s in-competition test had returned negative, said Irine Cheptai is set to be elevated to 2026 women’s champion.
The AIU said it also sanctioned two other high-profile Kenyan runners.
Veronica Loleo, a half-marathon silver medallist at the 2026 world road running championships, was banned for three years after testing positive for EPO in an out-of-competition test.
Meanwhile, Ronald Korir, who placed fourth in the 2023 Berlin Marathon, received a six-year ban after abnormalities were found in his athlete biological passport, which he failed to explain. The AIU analysed 20 blood samples taken from Korir from May 6, 2023, to August 18, 2025, and identified abnormalities.
“The Kenyan authorities have made a lot of progress in the fight against doping in the last five years, but these cases highlight that there is still a long way to go,” AIU chief executive Brett Clothier said in a statement.
“The Kenyan government is aware of the current situation and has committed to further strengthen the Anti-Doping Agency of Kenya and take action to address the criminal networks that facilitate doping within the country.”
These were the latest in a long series of doping cases involving distance runners from Kenya.
Women’s marathon world record holder Ruth Chepng’etich, also from Kenya, was banned for three years in 2025 after admitting a charge related to a positive test for a banned diuretic. Former New York Marathon winner Albert Korir was given a five-year ban in March.

noticias.titulo: Trump meets Putin and Xi for trilateral US, Russia, China talks at APEC
noticias.resumen: US president calls both Putin and Xi a 'friend' in separate meetings ahead of rare three-way talks in China.
noticias.texto:
Trump meets Putin and Xi for trilateral US, Russia, China talks at APEC
US president calls both Putin and Xi a ‘friend’ in separate meetings ahead of rare three-way talks in China.
United States President Donald Trump has met with his Chinese and Russian counterparts for highly anticipated trilateral talks at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit.
Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin met for a “family photo” before convening for talks on the sidelines of the summit in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday in an unprecedented gathering of the world’s three superpowers.
Opening the meeting, Xi said that it “has groundbreaking significance”.
“The world is at peace when great powers live in harmony,” Xi said, adding that the three countries “should work together to address global challenges”.
In a major statement, the Chinese leader also said “nuclear weapons should be comprehensively banned and thoroughly destroyed, building a nuclear-free world,” reported China’s Xinhua news agency.
In Trump’s opening remarks, the US president said the three countries are “uniquely positioned” to discuss nuclear weapons.
“Too often past leaders avoided talking to leaders they had disagreements with,” he said. “No peace ever forged by declining opportunities.”
Meanwhile, in his opening remarks, Putin made it clear that the war in Ukraine would be the focus of his conversation, before the three retreated into closed-door talks which lasted for about 55 minutes.
The talks between the leaders of the world’s largest nuclear powers were not likely to produce major agreements, analysts say, given deep differences over Ukraine, Iran, nuclear weapons and trade. But the meeting had unnerved smaller countries that feared their interests might be disregarded.
‘Special friendship’ between US, China
Ahead of the trilateral gathering, Trump held separate bilateral meetings with both Xi and Putin on Thursday.
The US president described Xi as a “friend” and said Washington and Beijing enjoyed a “special relationship”.
“As long as the two of us are in charge, I don’t think we’ll have a problem,” Trump said in opening remarks at his meeting with the Chinese leader. He also boasted that “no other countries can do what we can”.
Trump said the US has done “amazing” things in the past two years, since he returned to power, while praising China for many of its gains over several years.
Xi, meanwhile, said that he remained committed to working with Trump to steer ties between their countries on the “correct course”.
Relations between Beijing and Washington have been stable and improving, Xi said to Trump at the start of their third one-on-one meeting this year, which lasted for about an hour.
“We have established a new definition of a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability, giving it new substance based on respect, fairness and reciprocity,” Xi said.
Ahead of the bilateral meeting, Trump said the Board of Trade that he and the Chinese president agreed to form at their Beijing summit in May has brought balance to the two countries’ relationship. He said the US and China had split their tariffs in a “fair way”.
Putin ‘is my friend’
Earlier in the day, during talks with Putin, Trump also called the Russian leader a “friend”.
“We’ve had a great relationship for many years. We know each other for a long time, and I think a lot of wonderful things can come out of this, or at least start. But I think they’ll come out of this,” Trump told Putin.
A video published by the White House showed the two leaders shaking hands and Trump briefly whispering to Putin at the start of their meeting.
In another video posted by the White House Rapid Response X account, Trump was shown pointing at Putin and saying, “He’s my friend.”
Kremlin foreign policy aide Yury Ushakov said the two leaders “discussed the conflict in Ukraine and bilateral relations issues”.
“The meeting between the Russian and US leaders went well,” Ushakov said, according to Russia’s state news agency TASS, adding that Putin left the talks “in an excellent” mood.
‘High-stakes diplomacy’
Thursday also features the main event of the APEC summit, as representatives of the 21 Pacific Rim economies gather for discussions that will include high-stakes diplomacy, Al Jazeera’s Katrina Yu said, reporting from Shenzhen.
“Xi Jinping, who spoke at the banquet last night during the opening ceremony, said the discussion will centre on promoting mutual openness, innovation-driven growth and results-oriented cooperation,” said Yu.
On the US-China-Russia talks, James Bays, Al Jazeera’s diplomatic editor, said that when it comes to Trump, “his personal role always matters to him”.
But, he added, “something worth bearing in mind: you have three leaders here, Trump, Xi, and Putin. Putin has been in power; he’s been in the main driving seat in Moscow for 26 years; Xi’s been there for 14 years; and they know President Trump only has 26 more months.”
Speaking to Fox News earlier on Thursday, Trump highlighted the pomp surrounding his arrival. Xi greeted Air Force One on the airport tarmac on Wednesday, which contrasted with the more muted greetings offered to other leaders.
“This is a great president, one of the great presidents of China, and he’s never gone to the airport to meet somebody,” Trump said when asked what he wanted to get out of the trilateral summit.
Trump has insisted that nuclear arms control be a central topic of the meeting, despite Beijing’s repeated objections to talks on the issue with Washington and Moscow, which have far larger nuclear arsenals.

noticias.resumen: Is Trump helping rehabilitate Putin on the world stage?
noticias.texto:
Is Trump helping rehabilitate Putin on the world stage?
